t: Cross-Database Schema Mapper: a plain-language overview
title: Cross-Database Schema Mapper: a plain-language overview
description: Overview: what the Cross-Database Schema Mapper does and why archives need it. A cross-database schema mapper figures out which field in database A means the same as which field in database B: 'cust_name' here equals 'customerName' there. It compares names, types, and sample values to propose the mapping. Two different structures become one shared understanding.
provenance: Public methods compiled from standard information-extraction and knowledge-organization practice. Assembled for the JAH Databases archive.

t: How the Cross-Database Schema Mapper works
title: How the Cross-Database Schema Mapper works
description: Overview: what the Cross-Database Schema Mapper does and why archives need it. Real mappers score candidate field pairs by name similarity (edit distance, token overlap, synonym lookup), type compatibility (dates map to dates, not to free text), and value overlap on samples (both fields contain city names). High-scoring pairs become proposed mappings, conflicts (one field matching two) resolve by best-score-wins with the runner-up reported, and a human confirms the final map. The output is a field-to-field translation table with confidence per pair.
provenance: Public methods compiled from standard information-extraction and knowledge-organization practice. Assembled for the JAH Databases archive.

t: How the Cross-Database Schema Mapper works: the deep tour
title: How the Cross-Database Schema Mapper works: the deep tour
description: Overview: what the Cross-Database Schema Mapper does and why archives need it. Real mappers score candidate field pairs by name similarity (edit distance, token overlap, synonym lookup), type compatibility (dates map to dates, not to free text), and value overlap on samples (both fields contain city names). High-scoring pairs become proposed mappings, conflicts (one field matching two) resolve by best-score-wins with the runner-up reported, and a human confirms the final map. The output is a field-to-field translation table with confidence per pair. Advanced mappers use embedding similarity on field names and descriptions, learn from confirmed mappings to improve future ones, and handle structural mismatches (one field split into two, nested vs flat). Quality is measured by mapping F1 against expert-created gold maps. The limits are semantically tricky pairs ('name' as a person vs a product) and undocumented fields — those stay unmapped with their ambiguity noted rather than forced into a wrong pairing.
provenance: Public methods compiled from standard information-extraction and knowledge-organization practice. Assembled for the JAH Databases archive.
